title: Adaptive Eval Sentinel for Canary/A-B Rollbacks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an adaptive evaluation "sentinel" service that continuously monitors quality signals during canary and A/B rollouts and triggers automated rollback or mitigation policies. The sentinel will fuse model outputs, task-specific metrics, and distribution drift detectors across short and long windows to decide whether to pause, reduce traffic, or fully rollback a deployment. This ticket designs the signal set, decision engine, policy bindings, and integration points with the rollout controller and autoscaler.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel service ingests token-level logs and evaluation metrics (LL, BLEU-like task metrics, user-defined evaluation probes) from canary/A-B variants in near real-time.
Define configurable composite signals (quality_score, drift_index, latency_penalty) and mapping to actions (hold, scale-down, rollback, notify).
Policies support hysteresis, minimum evaluation window, cohort-aware baselines, and automatic fallback to safe model variant.
Integration tests simulate three failure modes (silent quality regression, input distribution shift, throughput-induced degradation) and sentinel triggers an automatic rollback in each case.
Dashboard displays per-cohort signal trends and a timeline of sentinel decisions; playback link to request traces for debugging.
description_more:
Motivation: We regularly see regressions introduced by config changes (quantization levels, compilation kernels) and new model variants that only manifest for particular cohorts or prompt lengths. Current canary gating is threshold-based and brittle: single-metric alerts cause noisy rollbacks or miss emerging regressions. The sentinel should combine multiple orthogonal signals and reason about short-term spikes vs sustained degradation, enabling safer automatic rollbacks with lower false-positive rates.

Scope: MVP focuses on hosted/runtime rollouts and dedicated pools. Private deployments will be supported later via a pluggable webhook decision endpoint. This ticket covers API/ingestion, signal definitions, decision engine (rules + simple ML ensemble), policy bindings, observability, and e2e tests.

Non-goals: full-blown offline eval suite, UI redesign, or custom per-customer policy authoring in MVP.
design_decisions: Use fused signals instead of single-metric gating: combine normalized quality_score (task evals), drift_index (KL-based on embedding distributions), and latency_penalty (P99/SLI breaches).
Decision engine = deterministic rules with weighted moving averages initially; later replaceable by a lightweight learned policy if needed.
Minimum evaluation window = 10 minutes or 1k requests, whichever is larger, to avoid reacting to microbursts.
Cohort-aware baselines: compute baselines per-customer, per-prompt-length bucket, and per-model-version to reduce false positives.
implementation_plan: 1) Instrument runtime to emit compact per-request evaluation events (request_id, model_variant, cohort_tags, prompt_len_bucket, ll, anchors).
2) Build sentinel ingestion pipeline (Kafka topic -> streaming aggregator) with 30s summarization granularity.
3) Implement signal calculators and normalization rules in Rust service behind a gRPC API.
4) Wire decision engine to rollout controller: actions = {hold, reduce_traffic, swap_variant, rollback, notify-sre}.
5) Add dashboard panels in Console and a 'why-rolled-back' request trace link.
6) Create chaos/regression tests and postmortem playbook for false positive rollbacks.
testing_plan: Shadow traffic tests in staging using recent production traces; inject synthetic regressions (lowered log-likelihood) and drift examples.
A/B smoke: 10% traffic to canary with sentinel enabled; verify automatic hold when composite score crosses threshold for >= two contiguous windows.
Load tests to ensure sentinel ingestion can handle 10k events/sec for a single cluster.
Golden path test: benign kernel change should not trigger sentinel within 60 minutes under normal variance.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive rollback causing customer-visible flaps. Mitigation: hysteresis, min window, and require two independent signals for hard rollback.
Risk: Metric poisoning by adversarial prompts. Mitigation: ignore known synthetic probes and require cohort agreement across multiple customers before rollback for public models.
Risk: Performance overhead. Mitigation: summarize at runtime, sample token-level details for debugging only on-demand.
